I kept the full rotation rather than a plain `n << d`. The plain shift gives the same results for the example calls, such as `left_rotate(16, 2) == 64`. But it drops the high bits instead of wrapping them around to the low end, so it isn't a rotation for values that use the top bits of the 32-bit word.

```python
def left_rotate(n, d):
    d %= 32
    mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
    n &= mask
    return ((n << d) | (n >> (32 - d))) & mask

assert left_rotate(16, 2) == 64
```

CONFIDENCE: 96
